title: RBAC: permissions + default roles for SIEM audit export management
creator: Ethan Park
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation — SIEM-ready audit export (Beta)
content:
Goal
Define least-privilege RBAC permissions required to manage SIEM-ready audit export configurations and to view delivery status/health in Console + API.

This work blocks:
- Control plane CRUD endpoints for export configs (ENG-5132)
- Console “Audit Export Settings” page (ENG-5177)
- Support workflows for token rotation + troubleshooting (runbooks / INT tickets)

Scope
1) Permission naming + semantics (API enforcement)
2) Default role mapping guidance (Enterprise Admin vs Auditor)
3) Ensure status/health endpoints are covered (view-only)
4) Ensure credential rotation is separated from config edit
5) Align with feature-flag gated rollout (beta allowlist)

Non-goals
- Fine-grained field-level access control within a single export config (e.g., hide destination host but show filters). We treat the destination details and filters as part of config visibility.
- Private/on-prem policy bundle differences (out of beta; capture as follow-up).

Background / constraints
- Export destinations include Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs, and S3 delivery. These require sensitive credentials (HEC token, DD API key, AWS role ARN / external ID) referenced via secrets manager, not stored in plaintext.
- Exporter has at-least-once delivery; downstream dedup is based on event_id (see delivery semantics ADR). Operationally, customers will ask “is it delivering?” which requires a status endpoint.
- Export config changes must be auditable (who changed what/when). This ticket focuses on RBAC, but we must not inadvertently block emission of audit events for export-management actions.

Proposed permission model (final)
We split permissions by resource and verb, and keep status/health read separate:

Resource: audit_export (per-tenant/workspace)
- audit_export.config:read
  Allows listing export configs and reading full config details including destination type, destination parameters, filters, and backfill window.

- audit_export.config:write
  Allows create/update/disable/delete export configs. Includes changing filters, enabling/disabling destinations, updating delivery format/partitioning for S3, and setting backfill window.

- audit_export.credentials:rotate
  Allows initiating credential rotation for an existing destination (e.g., update secret reference, re-validate). Does NOT allow changing non-credential fields (filters, backfill, destination host/index) unless audit_export.config:write is also present.

- audit_export.status:read
  Allows viewing delivery status (e.g., last_success_at, last_error_at, last_error_code/message redacted, export_lag_seconds, paused/auto-paused state) and per-destination health.

Notes:
- “write” is intentionally broader than “enable/disable” to avoid proliferating permissions during beta.
- Rotation is carved out since it is a common least-privilege ask: security ops wants to rotate tokens without having permission to alter what gets exported.
- Status is carved out because auditors/compliance often need read-only operational evidence.

Default role mapping (beta recommendation)
- Organization Admin / Workspace Admin: grant config:read + config:write + credentials:rotate + status:read
- Security Admin (if customer uses split roles): grant config:read + credentials:rotate + status:read (optionally config:write per customer policy)
- Auditor / Compliance Viewer: grant config:read + status:read
- Member / Developer: no permissions by default

Enforcement / API expectations
- Control plane endpoints must enforce the permissions on every request, scoped to tenant/workspace.
  - GET /audit-exports + GET /audit-exports/{id}: require audit_export.config:read
  - POST/PATCH/DELETE /audit-exports*: require audit_export.config:write
  - POST /audit-exports/{id}/rotate-credentials (or equivalent): require audit_export.credentials:rotate
  - GET /audit-exports/status (or /audit-exports/{id}/status): require audit_export.status:read

- “Test connection” flow in Console:
  - If it triggers an adapter validation using current credentials, treat as privileged action. We decided: require audit_export.credentials:rotate OR audit_export.config:write (either is acceptable). Rationale: it exercises the credential path and can generate outbound traffic; we should not permit for pure viewers.

- UI behavior:
  - Hide “Edit / Create / Disable” controls without config:write.
  - Hide “Rotate credentials / Test connection” controls without credentials:rotate or config:write.
  - Allow read-only status widgets with status:read.

Sensitive data handling
RBAC is necessary but not sufficient:
- Even with config:read, we must not return raw secrets (HEC token, DD API key). API returns secret references and a redacted marker only.
- Status endpoint must redact downstream responses that may contain tokens or customer URLs; return a bounded error_code + sanitized message.

Open questions (resolved)
1) Should config:read be required for status:read?
Decision: No. status:read can be granted independently. Reason: Some customers want NOC visibility of “is exporter healthy?” without granting full config details (destinations/filters may be sensitive). Status response must be carefully designed to not leak destination details.

2) Do we need separate permissions per destination type (splunk vs s3 vs datadog)?
Decision: Not for beta. Add as a GA hardening consideration if demanded.

3) Should delete require a separate permission?
Decision: No for beta; delete is guarded by config:write and feature flags + audit trail.

Implementation notes
- Add new permissions to policy bundle (rbac-policy-bundle) and map to default roles.
- Update authorization service to recognize these scopes.
- Ensure audit export API endpoints reference these checks (ENG-5132 owner to apply).

Acceptance criteria
- New permissions exist and are documented in the RBAC registry.
- Control plane endpoints enforce the correct permissions with tenant scoping.
- Default roles updated so Enterprise Admin can fully manage exports in beta.
- Auditor role (or read-only role) can view status without modification capabilities.
- Credential rotation is possible without config write.
- All permission checks covered by unit tests (positive + negative).

Links
- Control plane PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-28792-rbac-permissions-for-audit-export-management.json
- Policy bundle PR: sources/github/rbac-policy-bundle/pr-244-add-audit-export-permissions-and-default-roles.json
- Related API work: ENG-5132
- Console UI work: ENG-5177

Work log / updates
2025-02-04 (Ethan Park)
Created ticket. Need least-privilege model ASAP; several beta customers asked specifically about token rotation separation.

2025-02-07 (Kaitlyn Nguyen)
Drafted initial permission names (audit_export:read/write/status/rotate). Concern: too coarse; propose split config vs status and split rotate.

2025-02-10 (Marcus Lin)
Security review comment: status endpoints must avoid leaking destination hostnames/indices; allow status:read independent of config:read only if we keep status payload sanitized.

2025-02-12 (Sean Gallagher)
SRE ask: status:read must cover the same fields shown on dashboards (lag, paused state, last error time). Also ensure on-call can view status without needing config write.

2025-02-18 (Kaitlyn Nguyen)
Aligned naming convention with existing policy grammar: resource.subresource:verb (e.g., audit_export.config:read). Added test-connection permission rule (rotate OR write). Shared in #eng-platform for feedback.

2025-02-21 (Connor O'Brien)
Release note: ensure permissions ship before enabling beta allowlist; otherwise support cannot grant access cleanly. Also ensure feature flag doesn’t bypass RBAC.

2025-03-03 (Kaitlyn Nguyen)
Implemented permissions + role mappings in policy bundle; added unit tests. Opened PRs.

2025-03-10 (Ethan Park)
Verified control plane endpoints updated to enforce new scopes; no regressions in existing audit log read permissions.

2025-03-14 (Olga Petrov)
Compliance note: include wording that config changes are audited. Not directly in RBAC, but ensure export-management actions emit audit events (tracked in ENG-5132).

2025-03-21 (Kaitlyn Nguyen)
Merged policy bundle + control plane RBAC PR. Marking done. Follow-up suggested for GA: optional split permission for delete and per-destination management if demanded by customers.

Follow-ups
- Consider GA hardening: add audit_export.config:delete or require elevated role for deletion.
- Consider Private/on-prem differences (ENG-5202 scope).
